A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including the retained appendix plots and image galleries.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original domain-classifier evaluations, dataset-composition measurements, and CLIP and ResNet experiments, including domain-mixing and scaling results.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including Tables 1–12 and the performance plots.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the same FT natural-image classifier, DR-R rendition classifier, filtering procedure, and CLIP training approach. No algorithm, architecture, objective, or inference component changes.

E1.justification: The LAION-derived training datasets and ImageNet, ObjectNet, and DomainNet evaluations are retained. Newly cited datasets and research do not introduce additional evaluated domains or tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 5, 7, and 8 retain the same domain-classifier comparators and variants. The CLIP training-data comparisons and ImageNet-trained ResNet baselines also remain unchanged; newly cited methods such as SAFT and CLIPOOD are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Data splits, filtering thresholds, metrics, and training settings remain unchanged. Section 4 newly names the 4-million-sample subset, but the corresponding smallest-scale points already appear in v1 Figure 4; this clarifies an existing experiment.

E4.justification: The label-verification study, precision-threshold sweep, domain-mixing analyses, ResNet filtering comparison, per-shift robustness plots, and classifier error examples already appear in v1. The expanded discussion adds no new robustness experiment or supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed, and uncertainty reporting practices do not change. Both versions retain the same point estimates and annotator-agreement results, without adding confidence intervals or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Figure 6's caption changes the optimal rendition-to-natural ratio from 1:3–1:1 to 1:1–3:1, accompanied by explicit best-ratio annotations. Section 5 retains 1:3–1:1, creating an inconsistency. The tabulated benchmark scores and appendix results are retained.

T1.justification: The density-ratio formulation and relative corrected OOD accuracy definition remain unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: domain contamination explains much of CLIP's apparent generalization, clean datasets enable its assessment, and controlled mixtures reveal useful mixing ratios.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly argues that the findings, including optimal mixing ratios, should extend across architectures and losses, based on cited literature. Appendix A.9 adds labeling-bias and classifier-reliability discussion. Existing object-class and ambiguous-sample limitations are relocated rather than removed.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1.1 newly identifies all annotators as authors, and Section 4 explicitly documents the existing 4-million-sample setting. The code-access pointer changes from a repository to a project website. Training specifications and the resource-release statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds broader domain-generalization references, including Ben-David, WILDS, and invariant risk minimization, plus additional CLIP generalization papers. The introduction and discussion explicitly challenge assumptions in more prior works while retaining the original research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized introduction and discussion rewrites, corrects cross-references, and moves several discussion paragraphs into Appendix A.9. It also removes acknowledgements and author-contribution sections. The main narrative and methodological exposition remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves to the first page, affiliations move into a footnote, Figures 2–3 receive revised sample-grid formatting, and Figure 6 gains best-ratio markers and labels. All 12 tables and 34 figures remain, including the unchanged appendix galleries.

improvement.justification: v2 improves annotation provenance, literature context, and figure guidance. However, its revised Figure 6 caption gives an optimal ratio of 1:1–3:1 while Section 5 still states 1:3–1:1, leaving a highlighted finding internally inconsistent. These documentation gains and the unresolved numerical guidance do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
